Any Montana high school senior graduating in 2026 may apply if he or she will be attending an accredited institution of higher education. values.formattedValue: Open to MANRRS members and their children. High school seniors, college students or nontraditional students seeking funding to attend a two or four-year accredited college or university or technical school for any area of study may apply. Recipients will be selected based on academic records, social and community activities, and a typed essay describing personal and professional goals, and involvement with MANRRS. Two $1,500 scholarships will be awarded. Application Materials Needed: 1) Completed application form. Applications may be completed electronically through Google forms or by printing out and mailing the PDF form. 2) A copy of your most recent complete academic school year’s transcript. If you are a college student, you can send an unofficial copy of your transcript that includes the current school year in addition to the previous. 3) Letters of recommendation from a MANRRS leader of your choice AND from a teacher or professor. 4) Typed essay – three pages, 12-point Times New Roman font with one-inch margins. Application Deadline: April 1, 2026. Recipients will be selected and announced by July 31, 2026.

values.formattedValue: Scholarship awards $2,500 to high-achieving young women who are in their final year of high school and plan to attend an accredited postsecondary educational institution in the US or Canada in the next academic year. LEADERSHIP, ACADEMICS, EXTRACURRICULAR ACTIVITIES, COMMUNITY SERVICE and potential for future success are key attributes. There are 2 Whitefish chapters and each can nominate one outstanding young woman for consideration. To apply, the process needs to start THIS YEAR via interested JUNIOR GRADE women should send an electronic copy of their resume to either Chapter BR (peomtchapterbr@gmail.com) or Chapter D (PEOchapterD.MT@gmail.com) no later than May 15. After review of resumes, each local chapter will conduct brief interviews to determine a nominee who will, in turn, complete an online application to P.E.O. International for final consideration. The online application process can start as early as August 15 but no later than October 15. Nominees are notified of the outcome in mid-April of their senior year.

values.formattedValue: The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship, designed to provide recipients with the opportunity to graduate college debt-free. Applicants must attend a traditional public high school governed by a school district. Free workshops, Free Schwab Brokerage Accounts and Free Study Abroad provide recipients with a practical understanding of important life skills not typically covered in the school curriculum. (Hagan Scholarship Brochure). Applicant’s Adjusted Gross Household Income reported for 2023 Federal Income Tax Purposes must not have exceeded $100,000. “Household Income” is defined as the total income received by all members of a household living under the same roof. Applicants must show evidence they will be working 240 hours from January 1, 2026 to September 1, 2026 (they understand that most recipients work during the summer months. Work can be part-time during their senior year in high school or full-time during the summer or a combination of the two. They are looking for "students willing to contribute toward their educational expenses."

values.formattedValue:
JUST FOR WHITEFISH STUDENTS!!! The Kiita Foundation Scholarship (Kiita rhymes with cheetah) was established in 2023 by Jim and Jo-Ann Armstrong. They want to help a high achieving, financially independent student achieve a bachelor's degree. By financially independent, we mean someone who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college.  This award is very generous... up to $10,000 per year and renewable for up to 4 years. The recipient also has the opportunity to participate in all-expense paid service learning trips to Mexico with a cohort of other students.  They are looking for someone who is highly engaged in school and community activities. Again, they need to be financially independent when it comes to paying for college.  
The following essay questions: 1) This scholarship is for students who cannot rely on their family to help pay for college. Please explain why you need the assistance of this scholarship. 2) Please describe any obstacles in your path to high school graduation and how you have overcome them. 3) Please describe why you are interested in pursuing a bachelor’s degree and what you believe you are capable of achieving once you have earned your degree. You may explain this in terms of your life goals, career goals, and/or goals within your community. 4) Describe volunteer activities in which you have chosen to participate, why you chose those particular volunteer activities, and how those experiences have affected your life. Please contact Jill Seigmund at Whitefish Community Foundation with questions: (406) 863-1781 or jill@whitefishcommunityfoundation.org

values.formattedValue: The Big Sky State Games has teamed up with the CHARACTER COUNTS! Coalition and Mountain Alarm Fire and Security to recognize the importance of sportsmanship and character in Montana student athletes. CHARACTER COUNTS! is a nonprofit organization striving to improve the character of today’s youth. It is based on common ethical values that transcend political, religious, socio-economic, and cultural differences. Called the “Six Pillars of Character,” these values are: trustworthiness, respect, responsibility, fairness, caring and citizenship. Character Counts! Scholarship is sponsored by Mountain Alarm Fire and Security. Over the past twenty-four years, the Big Sky State Games has awarded the Character Counts! Scholarship to outstanding Montana female and male student-citizen-athletes involved in the Big Sky State Games. The scholarship can be used for any secondary education after high school. This includes trade schools and community colleges. Only high school juniors during the 2025-2026 school year are eligible for this scholarship. This is to ensure that fellow students can observe the scholarship winners during their senior year and to recognize the traits the students show. You can fill out the application below. It will also be available at all Montana High Schools Guidance Counselor offices.
